title: Gov.br PAdES (validation)
description: Gov.br signatures (advanced electronic signatures, Lei 14.063/2020) are made on Gov.br's own portal, as PAdES; SimpleSign does not make them, it validates them (the gov-br profile has no signing policy). This playbook validates PAdES files with the gov-br trust profile (the Gov.br AC roots bundled with SimpleSign.Brazil.GovBr and its chain validation) and its validation policy (the default's constraints, and a signing certificate without digitalSignature or nonRepudiation fails), through the library and the CLI. The signed files stand in for the portal's: the Sandbox signs them and its trust is added to the profile's (trustProfiles: Sandbox), so the checks show without a real Gov.br account; the first section shows that the profile alone trusts only the Gov.br chain. It complements sandbox-basics and etsi-baseline: what they already show (a changed document or signature value, a revoked, expired or untrusted signer, an unknown revocation status, raising a B-B to B-LTA and validating it after the certificate expired) is not repeated here; only what the gov-br profile and policy decide is.

inputs.title: A PDF signed on Gov.br's portal
inputs.description: Sign any PDF at the Gov.br signing service and upload what it hands back. The steps of the section 'A signature from the portal' validate it with the gov-br profile alone (the real Gov.br chain, no Sandbox), raise its level and add a second signer; without the file they are skipped.

sections.title: Files to validate
sections.description: PAdES signatures like the portal hands back: one or more signers of a PDF, with or without a visible stamp. Each one is validated right after with the gov-br profile and the Sandbox's trust.

steps.title: PAdES B-B, ETSI.CAdES.detached
steps.description: Signs the sample contract in PAdES B-B (ETSI.CAdES.detached) with a Sandbox certificate standing in for a Gov.br one, and validates it at once with the gov-br profile plus the Sandbox's trust. The trust steps validate this file.

steps.title: PAdES B-B, adbe.pkcs7.detached
steps.description: Signs in adbe.pkcs7.detached, the sub-filter the Gov.br portal writes, so the validation of that form can be shown without a real Gov.br signature.

steps.title: With a visible stamp
steps.description: Signs with a visible stamp in the portal's style (pt-BR date in Brasília time, 'Documento assinado digitalmente por', the ITI verification URL), to show the appearance stream does not affect validation.

steps.title: A second signer of the same PDF
steps.description: A second signer (RSA 3072) adds a signature to the signed-etsi file in a new field, in an incremental update: both signatures must stay valid, as on a PDF signed by two people on the portal.

steps.title: Signer with neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation (minimal signing policy, to validate)
steps.description: Signs with a certificate whose key usage has neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation, under the minimal signing policy and without validating, only to produce the file v-key-usage must reject.

sections.title: The Gov.br profile
sections.description: Its anchors are the Gov.br AC Raiz and intermediates; a chain that does not reach them is not trusted.

steps.title: Profile alone: the Sandbox's chain is not Gov.br's
steps.description: Validates the signed-etsi file with the gov-br profile alone: its anchors are only the Gov.br roots, so the Sandbox's chain is not trusted (NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND). Shows the profile does not accept just any CA.

steps.title: Profile with the Sandbox's trust added
steps.description: The same file with the Sandbox's trust added to the profile: the chain is trusted and the signature valid, and the ETSI TS 119 102-2 report must be valid against its schema. This is the setup the other validations use.

steps.title: ICP-Brasil's policy, trusting ICP-Brasil, Gov.br and the Sandbox
steps.description: A relying party that accepts both Brazilian signatures: one profile sets the policy, the others add their trust.

sections.title: Validation with the Gov.br policy
sections.description: The forms the portal produces (adbe.pkcs7.detached, a visible stamp, two signers) are valid under the Gov.br policy, through the library and the CLI; a signing certificate not meant for signing, the constraint that policy adds, is not. The cases any validator must reject (changed files, revoked, expired or untrusted signers) are in etsi-baseline and sandbox-basics.

steps.title: adbe.pkcs7.detached
steps.description: Validates the adbe.pkcs7.detached file under the Gov.br policy: the portal's sub-filter must be accepted.

steps.title: Visible stamp
steps.description: Validates the file with the visible stamp: valid like the invisible one.

steps.title: Two signers
steps.description: Validates the PDF signed twice: each signature covers its own revision and both must pass.

steps.title: Signer with neither digitalSignature nor nonRepudiation: not accepted
steps.description: The constraint the Gov.br policy adds to the default one.

sections.title: A signature from the portal
sections.description: The file uploaded for input:govbr-signed, made by Gov.br itself: its chain goes to the Gov.br AC Raiz bundled with SimpleSign.Brazil.GovBr, so only the profile's trust is used.

steps.title: Validate the portal's signature with the Gov.br profile alone
steps.description: An intact signature made on the portal, by a certificate that is valid and not revoked, is accepted under the gov-br profile and policy (without a signing-certificate attribute, which the portal does not write, the policy only warns).

steps.title: Validate it with the Gov.br policy, also trusting ICP-Brasil
steps.description: A relying party that accepts both Brazilian signatures: Gov.br's profile sets the policy (a missing signing-certificate attribute only warns), ICP-Brasil's adds its trust.

steps.title: Under the ICP-Brasil policy: no signing-certificate attribute
steps.description: The portal signs in adbe.pkcs7.detached without the ESS signing-certificate-v2 attribute, which the ICP-Brasil policy requires (as the ICP-Brasil signature policies do): under it the signer is not identified.

steps.title: Raise the portal's signature to B-LTA
steps.description: Raises the uploaded portal signature to B-LTA with the Sandbox's TSA, validating it with the gov-br profile alone: a real Gov.br signature can be preserved the same way.

steps.title: Add a second signer to the portal's PDF
steps.description: An incremental update after the portal's signature: the PDF keeps it intact and gains a signature made here.
